channel.title: Pier & Point · Building G
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for Building G (Mission Rock), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · Building G: The earlier row (2026-09-24) says the partitions "were permitted" for…
item.description: The earlier row (2026-09-24) says the partitions "were permitted" for $210,000. DataSF, permit 202308295553: "status":"approved","approved_date":"2024-02-22T09:47:47.000","issued_date":null,"description":"port mou: deferred free standing demountable partitions, aka dirtt (shop drawings). work on level 2,3,4". The permit is approved, not shown as issued, and is a deferred submittal of shop drawings. The same applies to the later row "Levels 2 through 4 of the office building were permitted for demountable partition walls." Both earlier rows are left as written. Source: https://data.sfgov.org/resource/i98e-djp9.json?permit_number=202308295553.

item.title: Correction · Building G: The earlier row (2026-09-22) says Via Aurelia is from Nayfeld "and Matt…
item.description: The earlier row (2026-09-22) says Via Aurelia is from Nayfeld "and Matt Brewer" and cites Appetito (2025-10-13) for over 200 seats and a bay view. KTVU, 2025-10-10: "Via Aurelia, the first upscale restaurant at Mission Rock, is now open on the ground floor of the Visa global headquarters"; "celebrated Che Fico chef David Nayfeld and his team at Back Home Hospitality". The page does not mention Matt Brewer or seat numbers, and the Appetito article is not in the row's sources. Only the opening by 2025-10-10 is supported by the page read. The earlier row is left as written. Source: https://www.ktvu.com/news/sfs-via-aurelia-restaurant-latest-open-fast-growing-mission-rock-development.

item.title: Correction · Building G: The 2026-09-22 row says Fieldwork held its grand opening, citing the…
item.description: The 2026-09-22 row says Fieldwork held its grand opening, citing the release's "Saturday, July 26" and noting July 26, 2026 was a Sunday. EIN Presswire, datelined July 28, 2026: "announce the grand opening of its 10th location ... on Saturday, July 26" and later "officially opens to the public on Monday, July 26". The release gives two weekdays for one date, and is the operator's own announcement. July 2026 is supported; the day is not. The earlier row is left as written. Source: https://www.einpresswire.com/article/929782480/fieldwork-opens-mission-rock-taproom-expanding-its-footprint-in-san-francisco.

item.title: Correction · Building G: The $60.4 million figure is the minimum Jobs Housing Equivalency Fee…
item.description: The $60.4 million figure is the minimum Jobs Housing Equivalency Fee required of Parcel G, the low end of a $60.4 million to $91.1 million range in the Phase 1 budget; the amount actually paid is not stated. Visa's company post of June 7, 2024 says nearly 1,000 employees had moved in to its new Market Support Center at Mission Rock. The Development Agreement took effect and the Disposition and Development Agreement was signed on August 15, 2018. LEED Gold is a stated target; no certification record has been found. Source: https://sfport.com/sites/default/files/Documents/Item%207A%20Mission%20Rock%20Phase%201%20Budget%20Approval%20%28003%29.pdf; https://corporate.visa.com/en/sites/visa-perspectives/company-news/mission-rock-market-support-center.html; https://sfplanning.s3.amazonaws.com/sfmea/2013.0208ENV-Seawall%20Lot%20337_NOD.pdf.

item.title: Correction · Building G: The Parcel G page no longer states that the building is Visa's global…
item.description: The Parcel G page no longer states that the building is Visa's global headquarters: a 2023 Port memo said it would be, while SF YIMBY (2024) and Fieldwork (2026) call it Visa's Market Support Center. The Port reported the office space 100% leased to Visa in April 2024; no source gives the lease signing date. Source: Port Commission Item 9A, 2024-04-05; Port Item 8B, 2023-10-06; Bisnow, 2019-11-06; SF YIMBY, 2024-09-05; SF Examiner, 2024-09-04; EIN Presswire (Fieldwork), 2026-09-09.

item.title: Correction · Building G: The Building G record now says Visa announced in June 2024 that it had…
item.description: The Building G record now says Visa announced in June 2024 that it had located its headquarters and global market support center in the building (SF Examiner, Sep 2024), instead of 'moved in April 2024', which was an expected occupancy date in an April 2024 Port memo. The 1,500-employee figure is labelled a planned capacity, and the 1051 3rd St address and the identification of an earlier lot as the Wharfside campus were removed as unsupported. Eight DBI permits now show their real filing dates and no 'issued' date, since DataSF records them only as approved. Blue Bottle is shown as announced (only pre-opening sources found); Proper Food and Fieldwork openings are stated as the sources give them; the Fieldwork opening is month-level because its release's 'Saturday, July 26' does not match the 2026 calendar; and Cybersource's registration is no longer shown as an opening. Architect credits, source titles and dates were corrected, and the Jan 30, 2018 approval now cites the Port Commission minutes. Source: San Francisco Examiner, 2024-09-04 (https://www.sfexaminer.com/news/business/sf-giants-partners-open-second-mission-rock-apartment-tower/article_7718b5d6-6af1-11ef-814c-63697129954c.html); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 9A staff report, 2024-04-05 (https://www.sfport.com/media/9595/download?inline=040924_9a_mission_rock_leasing_status_and_revised_phase_1_submittal_-_info_and_possible_action.pdf); BevNET (Fieldwork press release), 2026-07-28 (https://www.bevnet.com/pr/2026/07/28/fieldwork-opens-mission-rock-taproom-expanding-its-footprint-in-san-francisco); DataSF Building Permits; Port of San Francisco, Minutes of the Special Port Commission Meeting, 2018-01-30 (https://www.sfport.com/media/3353/download).
item.source: San Francisco Examiner, 2024-09-04 (https://www.sfexaminer.com/news/business/sf-giants-partners-open-second-mission-rock-apartment-tower/article_7718b5d6-6af1-11ef-814c-63697129954c.html); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 9A staff report, 2024-04-05 (https://www.sfport.com/media/9595/download?inline=040924_9a_mission_rock_leasing_status_and_revised_phase_1_submittal_-_info_and_possible_action.pdf); BevNET (Fieldwork press release), 2026-07-28 (https://www.bevnet.com/pr/2026/07/28/fieldwork-opens-mission-rock-taproom-expanding-its-footprint-in-san-francisco); DataSF Building Permits; Port of San Francisco, Minutes of the Special Port Commission Meeting, 2018-01-30 (https://www.sfport.com/media/3353/download)

item.title: Correction · Building G: The Mission Rock Phase 1 horizontal budget, Port Capital Advance and CFD…
item.description: The Mission Rock Phase 1 horizontal budget, Port Capital Advance and CFD bond figures had been duplicated identically across the cost entries of Parcels A, B, F and G. Each now appears once in the shared site-wide cost list (as public infrastructure investment for Mission Rock Phase 1), linked from each of the four records, since the Port's own memos name all four as sharing the budget. Parcel G's own appraised lease value and jobs-housing fee figures stay on its record, now labelled as land/lease and fee/subsidy costs specific to this parcel. Source: Pier & Point editorial decision.

item.title: Correction · Building G: Mission Rock Building G re-identified
item.description: Mission Rock Building G re-identified.
